headline: Inflation Jolt Leaves Stocks Broadly Lower, With Homebuilders and Energy Hit Hardest
body_html:
Stocks are under broad pressure on Tuesday. Of the 668 names in our universe, 531 are lower and only 127 are higher. Prices are not final, but the tone is clearly defensive after October inflation figures sent S&P 500 futures sharply lower, and a Reuters poll pointed to one more Fed rate increase in December.

No sector we track is in positive territory. Financials are holding up best, down 0.43%, followed by industrials at 0.67% and healthcare at 0.77%. Homebuilders are the weakest group, down 2.12%, which fits the rate worries. Energy is off 1.94% and semiconductors are down 1.23%, despite a softer tone in Gulf markets after talk of Iran strikes was dialed back.

Single-stock moves are outsized. AAON is the standout, up 16.34%, and Tokyo Electron has gained 9.07%. On the downside, Novanta has dropped 14.43% and Qualys 11.09%. Into the close, watch whether the 531 decliners stabilize or the selling accelerates. Traders will also be looking toward Wednesday, November 11, for any follow-through on rate expectations.

briefs.headline: Hot inflation reading rattles futures
briefs.body: S&P 500 futures fell sharply after the October inflation report, setting a cautious tone for the session. Within our universe, 531 stocks are lower against 127 higher. The reading revived worries that price pressures remain stubborn.

briefs.headline: Economists see one more Fed hike in December
briefs.body: A Reuters poll of economists expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates once more in December, citing persistent inflation risks. That outlook helps explain the pressure on rate-sensitive groups. Homebuilders are the weakest sector, down 2.12%.

briefs.headline: AAON surges more than 16%
briefs.body: AAON, the HVAC maker, is the biggest gainer in our universe, up 16.34% in a market where most stocks are falling. It stands well apart from the industrials group, which is down 0.67%. Traders will watch whether the move holds into the close.

briefs.headline: Chip-equipment names bounce against the tide
briefs.body: Tokyo Electron is up 9.07%, as the idea that markets bottom on bad news draws buyers to chip stocks. The wider semiconductor group is still down 1.23%, so the rebound is selective. The close will show whether the buying is durable.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity and photonics names slump
briefs.body: Qualys has fallen 11.09% and Novanta 14.43%, two of the sharpest declines in our universe. Software overall is down 0.96%, so the damage is concentrated in individual names. Furniture maker Ethan Allen is also down 10.02%.

briefs.headline: Gulf stocks rise as Iran strike talk cools
briefs.body: Gulf equities closed higher after Washington dialed back talk of strikes on Iran, even as diplomats say the U.S. will keep imposing costs on Tehran. Energy shares in our universe are still down 1.94%. Oil-market headlines bear watching into the close.
